data.source_title: BOASt - The Management of Distal Radial Fractures
data.source_setting: British Orthopaedic Association standard for skeletally mature patients with distal-radius fractures.
data.source_n: Not applicable; standard, no patient cohort.
data.quantity: Documented assessment and treatment decision factors
value: ulnar variance, intra-articular step, dorsal tilt
data.source_evidence_basis: BOAST says document injury mechanism and skin/circulation/sensation; for patients under 65 consider radiographic alignment and needs; age 65+ may favor non-operative treatment absent significant deformity or neurologic compromise; volar-displaced fractures are unstable.
data.limitations: UK standard, older than the AAOS 2020 guideline, and recommendations assume specialist clinical interpretation. Age is not a stand-alone patient value or local protocol.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Have the synthetic decision depend on injury, exam, post-reduction radiographs, functional needs, and clinician judgment rather than a single age threshold.

data.source_title: BOASt - The Management of Distal Radial Fractures
data.source_setting: British Orthopaedic Association standard for skeletally mature distal-radius fractures.
data.source_n: Not applicable; standard, no patient cohort.
data.quantity: Fracture-clinic review target and selective repeat imaging recommendation

value.repeat_imaging_condition: fracture believed unstable and subsequent displacement would lead to surgery
value.stable_fracture_mobilisation: consider removable support once pain allows

data.source_evidence_basis: BOAST recommends clinic assessment within 72 hours and radiographs at 1-2 weeks only when instability and management consequences justify them; it also calls for expected recovery/rehabilitation information and self-referral access.
data.limitations: These are UK service standards, not observed appointment times or a universal US follow-up schedule. No duration for pain resolution or total recovery is specified.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Model referral target separately from actual appointment; create conditional 1-2 week imaging only for unstable fractures when the result could change treatment. Keep recovery duration unknown.
